report.source_text: The computed tomography (CT) of the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis revealed the presence of a 23/19 mm (transverse) and 20 mm (cranial–caudal) mass lesion, respectively, having speculated margins, contrast enhancement, and areas of necrosis at the level of the dorsal segment of the right upper pulmonary lobe. The mass presented several extensions to the pleura and determined pleural invasion (Figs. 5 and 6). In addition, multiple mediastinal adenopathy were noticed, and some of them presented central necrosis.

clinician.final_diagnosis: pulmonary adenocarcinoma with lymph nodes metastases and paraneoplastic hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old man presented with chronic right shoulder and interscapular pain, clubbing of fingers and toes, swollen joints, and pachydermia. Chest CT revealed a 23x19 mm spiculated mass with necrosis and pleural invasion in the right upper pulmonary lobe, alongside necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies showed inflammatory syndrome, slight anemia, and markedly elevated VEGF supporting hypertrophic osteoarthropathy. Though histopathological confirmation was not documented, the clinical and radiologic findings strongly support pulmonary adenocarcinoma with lymph node metastases causing paraneoplastic hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient had chronic pain, clubbing, joint swelling, and skin thickening suggestive of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
Chest CT showed a spiculated necrotic mass with pleural invasion in right upper lobe and necrotic mediastinal lymph nodes
Laboratory findings revealed inflammatory syndrome, slight anemia, and elevated VEGF supporting diagnosis of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: benign causes of clubbing and joint pain
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Imaging showed a malignant pulmonary mass with metastatic lymphadenopathy.

Clinical course or treatment response linking paraneoplastic syndrome to the pulmonary tumor was not reported
